utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-04-75-T, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May we have the appearances, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, Douglas Stringer, Lisa Biersay, Case Manager Thomas Laugel, and legal interns Marija Knezevic and Marija Erceg.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Goran Hadzic, Zoran Zivanovic, Christopher Gosnell, with legal intern Paul Stokes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Mr. Bogunovic, Branko Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, good morning to you. May I remind you that you are still on your oath. Mr. Zivanovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something about what you said in your statement, a meeting in Velepromet in November 1991. I have information from a large number of participants in this meeting that it was chaired by a lieutenant-colonel of the JNA who introduced himself as the commander of the city of Vukovar. Can you confirm that, since you attended the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And I was also informed that at that meeting where the Croatian prisoners who had surrendered were mentioned, it was not mentioned where they were from at all, whether they were at the hospital or the barracks, wherever. Do you remember any of that? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said, among other things, that there were meetings that Goran Hadzic had with the then president of Serbia, Slobodan Milosevic. According to the information that I have, he had his first meeting with him when the Vance Plan was signed. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It seems to me that you took part in one of these meetings that were held, I think, in the presidency of the then SFRY where there was this discussion on the signing of this plan, where there were several participants in this discussion. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what I know and on the basis of the information I have, before that - that is to say, before this Vance Plan became a topical thing - Goran Hadzic had not had any contact with President Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say for sure. I don't think he had any, but I cannot say whether there weren't any meetings at all. Perhaps there was no need to have any meetings, and I believe that there weren't any meetings and that that happened only when all of us went together to attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the meetings concerning the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I also have information that he had a telephone conversation with President Milosevic when the cease-fire agreement was supposed to be signed. I think it was the 7th of September, 1991. And then he refused to sign that document because his office, his position was not referred to in that document. And then President Milosevic suggested to him that he sign it nevertheless. Do you perhaps know about that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. It wasn't that Goran decided this totally on his own. He consulted his colleagues, his assistants, wondering what to do, and we also thought that if you're not a proper official and if you're not there as a person who is there in a proper official capacity, then it shouldn't be signed. However, through this persuasion and also on the basis of this agreement reached with President Milosevic, the decision was made to sign it after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogunovic, yesterday, immediately at the outset, you said that you reviewed this statement that you signed. You said how focused you were and what you did notice and what you did not notice. Yesterday you were providing answers and today you're answering as well. What about now, were you focused when giving these statements before the Court here, now?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I try to be as focused as possible. I tried to give accurate answers. Or, rather, to say what it was that had actually happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to put one more question to you. If we were to find certain contradictions between what you said yesterday and today, here, before this Court, on the one hand, and on the other hand what is written in your statement, would you say that what you're saying today is something that we should treat as the truth?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: One moment. Just one moment, Mr. Bogunovic. Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I am objecting to this question. The assessment about truthfulness will be made by this Trial Chamber, and I think posing this question to the witness is improper and meant to be coaching, and I strongly object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is not the question of assessment. I don't ask the witness to assess his statement but to tell us how he looks at some inconsistencies between his testimony yesterday and today and the allegations from his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, this question is way too general and not fair to the witness. If you have specific instances to show where, in your view, there is a contradiction, you can put a question to the witness but not in general what -- when did you tell the truth. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, this is what I'm going to put to you. For instance, in your statement -- well, let me start with the last thing. You said that Goran Hadzic met with Milosevic several times in 1991, I mean from January onwards, during 1991. Today you said that you allow for this other possibility; namely, that in actual fact he first met with President Milosevic personally when the Vance Plan was topical. So tell us, what can we rely upon, upon what you said today or upon what is contained in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: As --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Excuse me. Thank you, Your Honour. I believe the Court saw me standing well into the question because I saw exactly where it was going, and it's again trying to get at the same effect but in a different way and we object to it. It is not for this witness to say. It is for this Court to assess which statement is truthful, not for him to assess the issue of inconsistencies, if any.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It is very specific question about the parts. If necessary, I could show the witness the specific paragraphs, but as far as I know, the Prosecution did not deny that it stands in his statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It is not for the Prosecution to deny that something is in his statement. It is the Defence's responsibility to direct the witness to the information that they would like to discuss with the witness. This is not for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, could you remind us of the date of the signing of the Vance Plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The date of signing of Vance Plan is the 23rd of November in Sarajevo, but their meetings were in December --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: November? Pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You may continue, Mr. Zivanovic. And, Mr. Bogunovic, if you remember the question, you may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you wish, I'm going to remind you of the question that I put. Actually, in your statement it says that you said that during 1991, from January onwards, Hadzic met with President Milosevic. Today you said that you allow for this other possibility, that it happened when the Vance plan was being discussed sometime in 1991. In view of all of this, these two different things, what do you do you think is true? What do you do you think is correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic, before the witness answers, could you direct us to where in the statement this precision of from January on is to be found?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. This is paragraph 17 and it is in paragraph 14 -- paragraph 14, paragraph 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zivanovic, you can't ask the witness which of the statements is true, so please rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether the first personal meeting between Hadzic and Milosevic took place then, when the Vance Plan was discussed - that is to say, in November, December 1991 - or whether it happened before that, from January 1991 onwards?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I'm sure - and I know, because I was present myself - when the Vance Plan was being discussed and when we were in Belgrade. However, what Goran said to us -- in the Krajina, in the Slavonia, Baranja area, there were many people who were afraid. People were asking for weapons, for help. They were seeking safety and security. I'm convinced that Goran, on several occasions, said, "No problem, I agreed all of this with President Milosevic." Although, to tell you the truth, I wasn't sure whether he had been with him then or not, but he said it in order to alleviate the situation as it was at that moment. That's probably why he said it. I cannot claim that he was or that he was not, because I did not know. He did not tell anyone that officially. He did not say, "Yes, I was there at such and such a date and this is what happened," and so on and so forth. I think that this was said to calm these people down so that there wouldn't be any -- well, how do I put this? So that people would not lose confidence in themselves, in us, and in order to prevent something that had already happened, namely, when women and children from that area crossed over to Serbia and they were there for about a month until the situation calmed down. So I am not sure, I cannot tell you whether Goran was there or not. I mean, he did mention, he said, "Don't worry, don't worry about a thing, I agreed upon all of this with President Milosevic." But again I'm saying I don't know whether he spoke about this on the phone or whether he went to see him personally: That's the way it was. Now, I cannot say to you at all whether this is correct or not. Both possibilities are there and I cannot opt for either one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It says here, among other things, that you said that when the Serbian National Council was being established in January 1991, or between January 1991 and August, he had met with Milosevic five times. Does that mean, in fact, that you don't know exactly whether they had meetings or not? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat this: I was not with him, so I cannot confirm that, yes, they did meet so -- and so many times. There was a time, on the 1st and the 2nd May, when Borovo Selo was attacked and people were already panicked by that time, they feared for the future of their children and everything, and then there was a meeting or a discussion or I don't know what with Mr. Milosevic. But again, I cannot maintain that Goran met with Milosevic or didn't meet with him. I suppose he did, but I cannot say with 100 per cent certainty that, yes, he met him and I was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the transcript missed one thing and that is that I referred to paragraph 15 of his statement. [In English] Sorry, may I consult my client for the moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. Is it the case that in some talks or some discussions you and the others had, perhaps it was misinterpreted when Goran Hadzic said that he had been in Belgrade and you understood it as him having talked to President Milosevic. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such cases when he came and said, "I have been in Belgrade and talked to Milosevic," but I must say that on a couple of occasions his report was not accepted as such. We doubted that he had actually done that because there were no results. Nothing happened. So we began to doubt that he had indeed been to Belgrade and had that contact and had that discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogunovic. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, redirect?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I could just have a few seconds to set up.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to yesterday to some questions that you answered for Mr. Zivanovic. I sometimes will mention a transcript page and that's not meant for you. It's for the record. I don't expect you to know what the transcript pages are. At transcript pages 9143 to 9145, you described a meeting happening in Borovo Selo with the then minister of the interior of Croatia, Mr. Boljkovac, do you recall that exchange with Mr. Zivanovic yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And specifically, you said: "I said to them, I suggest to you that we go to Borovo Selo and I have a staff there." And you explained that they accepted the proposal and you did go to Borovo Selo, and you said: "We were met there in the traditional Serb way with bread and salt." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you describe who the participants were at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the municipality where I came, there was Savo Davidovic on the Serbian side from Brsadin, Mr. Mercep from the Croatian side, and the chief of police from Vukovar. There was Mr. Slavko Degoricija, prime minister of Croatia. Mr. Boljkovac, minister of the interior of Croatia. And a couple of people I honestly didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who was there from the staff that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Well, you said that you proposed to go to Borovo Selo, that you had a staff there --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- and so it's that staff --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- that I wanted to know which members actually attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak into the microphone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean when we already went to Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, can you please speak into microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. Bogunovic, could you move your chair forward? It may be more comfortable for you.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about who met me in Vukovar and with whom I spoke in Vukovar. After that, we went to Borovo Selo where the Main Staff was, the headquarters, that decided on many things that were happening at that time in the Slavonia, Baranja area. And I said that at the Main Staff we found Vukasin Soskocanin, the commander of the staff, and a couple of more people who happened to be there and who were involved in these discussions where we were trying to decide what to do next.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the record, when you say "Main Staff," Main Staff of what?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not exactly a Main Staff. It was the headquarters for Borovo Selo, which had about 11.000 population, the largest village in the area. And we tried to come to a decision --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- together with them what to do. All the other villages were smaller. They had smaller staffs or headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I understand. My question to you is: When you said yesterday that you had a staff there in Borovo Selo and when you said just a few seconds ago where the Main Staff was, I'm asking you the Main Staff of what. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Main Staff? Well, their decision was passed on to all the other staffs that existed in every village. There was a Crisis Staff in every village looking after the population. And what was decided in the Borovo Selo staff was passed on to all the other villages and accepted in the entire Slavonia, Baranja area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And -- excuse me. One moment, Mr. Bogunovic. Could you describe for us in what time-frame this meeting happened, the one where you were met in the traditional Serb way?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some time in May 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I see. At transcript page 9194, you mention that Jan, and the name is written phonetically, and I wondered if you could help us spell it, it's Jan Kisgeci, who was calling every day to ask about problems with Slovaks. Do you know how to spell that name?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which name was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: The first name is Jan, the minister of agriculture from the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kisgeci, K-i-s-g-e-c-i.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, yesterday, Mr. Bogunovic, at transcript pages 9145 to 9146, you and Mr. Zivanovic discussed Grahovac, Slobodan Grahovac and Dusan Filipovic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, you said that you understood Grahovac to be someone who was responsible to someone else to whom he reported. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bogunovic, before I continue, I wanted to take one step back. Yesterday you testified that you had had several opportunities to review this statement; is that correct? That's what you testified to yesterday? Do you recall saying that to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And do you recall that you've also given other statements to representatives of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I remember the statements that I have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you recall testifying in the Stanisic and Simatovic case?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And, in fact, for your preparation for your testimony here yesterday and today, you reviewed that testimony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now if I could direct your attention to Exhibit P3204.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And may I have some assistance in giving to Mr. Bogunovic this hard copy of his statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would object. This is not on the Prosecution list.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Oh, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But this --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did I give you the wrong one? This is his statement dated September 2012, which was admitted yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: It's the same one. Would you like to see it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And if I could direct your attention to paragraph 86, which is on page 17. I will read it because it may be difficult to find the sentence that I'd like to direct your attention to. "Appointed as the Minister of the Interior in August 1991, my first duty was to form police stations in the villages of Borovo Selo and Dalj. In the Ministry of Interior, there was only a public security section and I was in charge of it. There was a separate state security that was directly subordinated to Goran Hadzic. At an SAO SBWS government meeting in December 1991, we were informed that the security service had been formally established. Hadzic called it the Security Service and it functioned based on orders given by Hadzic. Even though the Security Service was not formally established yet at the end of October 1991, Goran Hadzic sent Dusan Filipovic and a man whose last name was Grahovac to Sid. I believe they were part of Hadzic's Security Service because they were well-informed about me and the people around me." Have I read that correctly, Mr. Bogunovic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you read that correctly. However --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Bogunovic --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I see here that they --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, one moment. I haven't yet put a question to you. I just wanted to know if I had read that correctly. And I did, did I?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So is it correct, as written in your statement, that Goran Hadzic was the one who sent Dusan Filipovic and Grahovac to Sid?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, Dragan Grahovac - now I remember his name - and Dusan Filipovic were employees of the security service of Serbia. It was in fact Badza's team. I believe that Goran met them first when Badza brought them to Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: My --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I think is most probable.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: My question to you is: Is it correct, as written in your statement, that Goran Hadzic sent Dusan Filipovic and Grahovac to Sid? Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I think it would be appropriate to let the witness answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I have just put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zivanovic -- Mr. Bogunovic, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So were you truthful and accurate when you said Goran Hadzic sent Dusan Filipovic and a man whose last name was Grahovac to Sid?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that at the time. However, now, after everything and after some things that I learned, I doubt they were sent by Goran Hadzic. I believe that was done by Radovan Stojicic, Badza. I believe it was on his orders that they went there.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So the new information that you got happened after you signed this statement in September of 2012. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I realised that yesterday during our discussion, that Badza had arrived with 11 people or so. I thought it was three or four men and these men did not belong to our structures.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: But let me --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understood, Filipovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Let me show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we may have tab 120, which is 65 ter number 29 -- excuse me, it's actually an admitted exhibit, 2979.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bogunovic, on the first page can you see number 15, the name that's there on the first page? Excuse me, Mr. Bogunovic, if you could look on your screen before you, are you able to see it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Do you see the name Grahovac, Slobodan, at number 15?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And underneath, do you see the name Filipovic, Dusan?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dusan Filipovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And next to Grahovac, Slobodan, do you see SOSB ZS?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could we please go to the next page. And could we please highlight the paragraph that's right under the word "minutes"?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I will read it to you in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: If we could please go back to the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: "Minutes from a meeting of the commanders of the Territorial Defence and representatives of the villages of Lovac, Opatovac, Sotin, Tovarnik, and Mohovo, with the deputy minister of the Serbian district and members of the Main Staff of the Serbian district. The meeting is attended by:" And do you see the word "Slobodan" underneath?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So according to this document, these people are having a meeting and the meeting has been attended by commanders of the TO and representatives of the villages listed. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We can remove this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Ms. Biersay, perhaps we should clear up something with regard to the first name of Mr. -- what's his name again?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Slobodan Grahovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Grahovac. Because at page 15, line 24 of the transcript, in his answer to one of your questions, the witness said: "Well, you see, Dragan Grahovac, now I remember his name, and Dusan Filipovic were employees," et cetera. Now, is this Mr. Slobodan Grahovac the same person we are talking about now or is it a different person?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, yesterday you described that there was -- Filipovic and Grahovac were always together. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether this person's name that's also at the same meeting with Dusan Filipovic, the name Slobodan Grahovac, is that the person who was always with Dusan Filipovic? You're nodding but we have to write it down, so we have to hear what you have to say.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is one more Grahovac but in Vukovar, that is Dragan Grahovac in Vukovar. So I confused the two for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now I'd like to move to another topic. At transcript page 9172, you testified yesterday that: "Our lives," meaning the lives of the -- I think, the government, "would have been easier, much easier, when there were no Badzas and no Arkan." Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at transcript page 9163, you confirmed that Badza was the commander of the Territorial Defence of the SBWS, and this you did in your conversation with Mr. Zivanovic. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At this time, may I please have tab 5 on the screen which is admitted as L38.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: We're just waiting for the document to come on the screen, Mr. Bogunovic. Now, this is the minutes of the 17th session of the government of the Serbian District of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, held on 19 November 1991 in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I'd like to move to the third page, specifically I'm looking for item 2. It's the third page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I'll read this. "Goran Hadzic, president of the government, briefed those present about the current situation from the international point of view, and the talks which had been held with the representatives of the Republic of Serbia and the Yugoslav People's Army. Radovan Stojicic briefed those present on the military situation. The following took part in the discussions," and there is a list of names. The next sentence begins: "A unanimous decision was reached that the commander of the Territorial Defence had their full confidence, and that his status had been established by the decision of the Great People's Assembly which proclaimed that units of the Territorial Defence form a part of the Yugoslav forces." And my question to you, Mr. Bogunovic, this affirms that the government had full confidence in Stojicic. Does it appear to you in this item that they were condemning him in any way for anything that he had done?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you quite frankly, I was not in favour of that, that is to say, to have this person appointed to that position. However, since the majority wanted that, of course I had to accept it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Bogunovic, at page 9175 of yesterday, the transcript page, you describe that Badza was the one who dismissed this Cizmic who was commander of the Dalj police station. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to now ask that tab 14, which I -- I believe there is a public redacted version. It may be best not to broadcast it, but I think there is a public redacted version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'm just asking for a document to be put on your screen. And while we're doing that, if you could look at your statement, Mr. Bogunovic, which you have there, the statement that you have. If you could go to paragraph 124.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I think it's Exhibit 119.111.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: My question to you is: Did you -- how soon after this was signed, which is on the 2nd of October, 1991, how soon after that did you hear about the removal of Cizmic from the police station? Because you describe hearing about it yesterday, and I wanted to know how soon after his removal did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly now, but when I first came to Erdut to attend a meeting, I heard that Cizmic had been dismissed from the position of commander of the police station in Dalj and that he was dismissed by Lazic and Dragan Djukic, that they replaced him on orders from Zavisic or, rather, Badza.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And now this is dated October 1991 which -- this dismissal happened before the government gave him their full confidence in the document we saw previously; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Badza?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: One minute, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- although --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- Mr. Bogunovic, I have a very limited amount of time. I'm trying to be very specific with my questions, and so I would appreciate it if you answered my questions --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- that I ask specifically.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And so my specific question is: This dismissal happens in October 1991 and the full confidence that's given to Badza happens in November of 1991. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the contents of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- the document of the minutes from 20 of November were misrepresented to the witness. He got just the confidence in one area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Is Mr. Zivanovic testifying? I'm sorry, I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. It is my objection. And I could say it and I could explain it, but not in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I -- that's fine, Your Honour. I'll move on to another topic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: At transcript page 9158, Mr. Bogunovic, you describe that you were told to keep in touch with Badza because he was -- this is what is in the transcript, so you won't find it in your statement. You describe that you were told to keep in touch with Badza because he was from MUP Serbia. Do you recall telling Mr. Zivanovic that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And who told you to keep in touch with Badza because he was from MUP Serbia?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I came to Erdut to attend this meeting, I was told, I mean, Goran told me and some other people told me that Badza had come there as an employee of the MUP of Serbia and that I have to have contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And this document doesn't have a tab number. It was not on our list from -- that we sent. And this is P251.245. And this arises from Mr. Bogunovic's testimony yesterday regarding Badza's involvement in the dismissal of Cizmic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this document is not on the list of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, but Ms. Biersay gave the reason why she's calling that document, which is specific for redirect, I think. Wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I'll -- this is a --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'll read this document. It's dated 16 October 1991: "During its session held on 16 October 1991, and in accordance with Article 2, paragraph 1, item 6 of the Law on the Government of the Serb Region of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, the Government of the Serb Region area of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem has passed a decision on the dismissal of the secretary of the Vukovar Secretariat of Interior. "Janko Milakovic shall be dismissed from his position as the Secretary of the Vukovar Secretariat of the Interior ..." And it has the name -- do you recognise the name at the bottom of that, Goran Hadzic? Do you see that on your screen, this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So this document was not signed by Badza, was it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Was it signed by Badza or is it signed by Goran Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a video that I'd like to play. The video is actually a video of Mr. Bogunovic testifying in the Stanisic/Simatovic case. We have the transcripts on the 65 ter exhibit list, 65 ter 4466 and 67, but as the Court is well aware, transcripts are not available in Mr. Bogunovic's language. So the idea is to have him listen to the video in his language and have it interpreted for the rest of us. And the interpreters have been provided copies of the transcripts, which are 65 ter number 4466 and 4467.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: There is no objection, so please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Before I turn to your Stanisic and Simatovic testimony, Mr. Bogunovic, you testified in 2010; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And at that time you had not been -- you had not yet committed the crime for which you were convicted; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So you testified before all of those events?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mr. Hadzic was a fugitive from this Tribunal before he was arrested by this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard something but I'm not sure. I mean, that it was that time and that -- that he was wanted as a fugitive.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Did you know that Mr. Hadzic was arrested by this Tribunal in July of 2011?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that. It was on television and I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So what I'd like to now address is the information that you provided the Trial Chamber yesterday and today about what Mr. Hadzic told you and what you knew about Stanisic, Jovica Stanisic and Slobodan Milosevic. Do you recall discussing those issues with Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So at this time I'd like to turn to -- on paper it's 65 ter number 4466, and the transcript pages run from 5972, line 1, to 5973, line 19, and they will correspond to the video at 25 minutes and 2 seconds to 30 minutes and 26 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So at this time, Mr. Bogunovic, I am going to play this testimony for you and I want you to listen to it very carefully.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voice-over] "A. I became aware of it during a meeting when Goran told all of us that he had been to Belgrade and that he had an agreement with President Milosevic to go on with our work and establish a government. He also said that we enjoyed their support and that everyone was aware of that. "Q. How often would Goran Hadzic go to Belgrade to meet with Slobodan Milosevic between January 1991 and the formation of the SAO SBWS government in August of 1991? "A. That was on several occasions. On several occasions he conveyed a message to us. I'm not sure he informed us about all of his visits, but those visits probably happened five or six times during that period of time. "Q. When did you first hear of Jovica Stanisic being present at these meetings in Belgrade? "A. Well, I heard that. Goran told us. He told us that he went to visit President Milosevic together with Jovica Stanisic. "Q. Approximately when did Goran Hadzic tell you about this meeting with Jovica Stanisic and President Milosevic? "A. He told us that on the eve of the setting up of the SAO Krajina government. "Q. Did you hear of Jovica Stanisic being present at all meetings held from January 1991 to August 1991? "A. Well, as far as I could learn from Hadzic who informed us about what was going on, yes. "Q. When is the earliest point in time that you heard of Jovica Stanisic being present at meetings in Belgrade? "A. Well, I heard that sometime after the 1st of May, after the conflicts broke out in Borovo Selo. That was when he informed us that Jovica Stanisic had also attended a meeting. "Q. Between May and August 1991, how often did Hadzic go to Belgrade for these meetings? "A. I think -- or, rather, as far as I know from his reports during that period, he attended such meetings about four times, meetings in Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: For the record, I believe the English translation for the -- our transcript here today began at page 5972, line 13, of 65 ter number 4466, so I will just read the few lines before then. "Q. Between the formation of the SDS party in May of 1990 and the establishment of the Serb National Council on 7th January 1991, did you become aware of any communications between Goran Hadzic and Slobodan Milosevic? "A. Goran Hadzic mentioned going to Belgrade and he said that there he would meet Slobodan Milosevic. He would then convey that to us during various meetings. "Q. In paragraph 15 of Exhibit P554," and for the -- "... you state that Goran Hadzic went to Belgrade a number of times during 1991 to meet with Stanisic and with Slobodan Milosevic." And it quotes that section of the exhibit. "I know that because in government meetings Hadzic often mentioned these meetings." The question was posed to the witness: "When did you become aware of Hadzic going to these meetings in Belgrade in 1991?" And after that he answered: "I became aware of it during a meeting when Goran told all of us," and I believe the rest was translated.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, did you recognise yourself in that video that we just played?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And was that testimony that you gave truthful?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I said what I knew and what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is to say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, I would like to hear the witness's answer in its entirety, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, shall I read what you just said and then there was an end. You said -- I asked you whether that testimony was truthful, and you said: "I think that I said what I knew and what I heard ..."

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that is what I could say at that moment, because I had not known of anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. President, are you satisfied with -- okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I am, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I'd now like to play another clip, and this is also from your Stanisic, Simatovic testimony. And on paper it's 65 ter number 4466, from transcript page 5995 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We'd like to know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- whether the Prosecution impeach its own witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay, I think, although the translation is not complete, that Mr. Zivanovic asks or wants to know whether you impeach your own witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I am pointing out to the witness his previous statement, leaving it up to him to tell us whether it was truthful or not and he has done so. I am seeking to show that the leading questions asked yesterday and today by Mr. Zivanovic got imprecise and sometimes information, yes, that was -- that is inconsistent with what he has said previously. So I am seeking to corroborate his statement and not to impeach him to that extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And so at this time if we could go to the second clip. And as I was saying, it goes from transcript page 595 -- 5995, line 12, to 5996, line 24. And the tape runs from 21.36 to 25.06.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bogunovic, I'll play another clip and if you could listen once again to this, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Q. In your previous statements you describe personally meeting with Jovica Stanisic on three to four occasions. In paragraph 14 of Exhibit P554, you discuss a late August 1991 meeting in Novi Sad in the Vojvodina building -- excuse me, in the building of the Vojvodina police. What is the reason that you and Hadzic went to this meeting in Novi Sad? "A. The reason we went to Novi Sad was the setting up of police stations in Dalj and Borovo Selo. We went there to discuss getting uniforms for the police, small arms and rifles, as well as means of communication and a couple of vehicles that would be used by our police. "Q. In paragraph 13 of Exhibit P553, you state as follows: "'Radovan Stojicic, also known as Badza, was with the Serbian MUP, acted as co-ordinator and gave us guidelines on what to do. He was the one who said we could go to Novi Sad and get the uniforms and equipment.' "How did Badza co-ordinate that meeting in Novi Sad? "A. Badza co-ordinated the meeting through Goran Hadzic. He told him that we should go to Novi Sad and that I should go as the minister of the interior, and we were supposed to discuss the hand-over of all the aforesaid things. "Q. Was this meeting the first time that you met Jovica Stanisic in person? "A. I am not sure whether that was the first or the second time. I believe it was the first time. "Q. Approximately how long did this meeting in Novi Sad last? "A. The meeting was rather short. The decision was made to give us what we had requested. Near Novi Sad there is a place called Klisa, there was a police depot there. Some ten or 15 minutes after that meeting I already went to that place, Klisa, and they began to deliver to me the uniforms and all the other things that I mentioned. "Q. Who did this police depot belong to? "A. To the MUP of Vojvodina; specifically, the regional secretariat in Novi Sad. "Q. Okay. And the MUP of Vojvodina is a part of which MUP? "A. The MUP of Serbia. "Q. Could you please describe the uniforms that were provided to you for the police forces of the SAO SBWS? "A. The uniforms were the same as the uniforms worn by the Serbian police, the police of Serbia. Trousers, shirts, short-barrelled weapons, just like the police in Serbia."

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And I'll put the same question to you, Mr. Bogunovic. Is that information -- that testimony that you gave before the case in Stanisic and Simatovic, was that accurate and truthful?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Does it refresh your recollection about the timing of the Novi Sad meeting where you met Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the beginning of October 1991. I'm not sure but I think that's when was it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a -- Your Honours, I have another short clip, and I was just looking at the time and wondered if the Court would prefer to take the break a few minutes early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If you -- if this is an appropriate moment --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- for you. We'll take a break, then, until 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: -- Your Honours. This is a brief oral submission in respect of the procedure that was followed before the break in terms of putting portions of a --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Well, it's not an objection. It's a proposal that we have this discussion, perhaps, outside the presence of the witness or without him wearing his headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I'm informed the witness doesn't speak English, so I believe removing the headphones would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Or, on the other hand, we could also wait until he's finished testifying. I don't -- I have, perhaps, four or five more questions and I don't know if this is something that needs to be done with the witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The reason I rose now, and I -- I, of course, I am loath to do it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And again, this is being translated, I believe, to the witness, and I just wonder if it's prudent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you to take off your headphones, please. Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: The reason I did so now, Mr. President, is because the timeliness of the objection may be an issue, so I wish to put this on record as soon as I possibly could when my learned friend and I became aware of the state of the law in respect of the manner in which the witness was being questioned by the Prosecution. And, Your Honours, if I may just direct you to a very brief passage of an Appeals Chamber judgement -- decision from the 1st of February, 2008, in the Popovic case. And, Your Honours, I won't take you through this in detail, but I just wish to give you the few sentences that are relevant. The Appeals Chamber there, in respect of a Trial Chamber oral decision, said: "The Trial Chamber's practice to date, as well as that of other Trial Chambers, demonstrates a general, if not altogether consistent approach, that puts the decision to allow a party to put a prior statement to its own witness and cross-examine that witness in the hands of the Trial Chamber. This may or may not be done on the basis of a prior determination of hostility. In this light, the Appeals Chamber considers that the Trial Chamber's decision to put the determination to impeach in the hands of the calling party constitutes a discernible error. It further considers that the Trial Chamber committed a discernible error in deciding to leave the scope of the challenge to the discretion of the impeaching party. It may be that the Trial Chamber will decide to allow a calling party to put a prior inconsistent statement to its witness in order to clarify a particular contradiction without declaring the witness hostile. The interests of justice dictate a certain measure of flexibility. However, this again will be a matter for the Trial Chamber to determine in the circumstances before it." Now, Mr. President, what I interpret that to mean is that when a party wishes to put a prior statement of a witness to its own witness for the purpose of showing an element that is different to what has been adduced, then that in substance is impeachment, and I believe that my learned friend opposite candidly indicated that to some extent that was indeed the purpose of showing the prior statements from the Stanisic case. And what I suggest this instruction from the Appeals Chamber indicates is that it is for Your Honours to decide whether that should be permitted and to specifically determine the basis and the scope of the questioning that is permitted. And why is that? Because it's a departure from the traditional principles of examination and cross-examination, and the Appeals Chamber discusses the foundation and the policy factors for its final conclusion. Now, it's true that we on this side of the courtroom didn't stand up and assert a vociferous insistence that Your Honours make such a determination, but we do so now. We do make that insistence. And we would also ask that as a remedy for the -- for what has occurred, that -- in terms of presenting these prior portions of the witness's statement, we would ask -- if Your Honours determine that you did -- were assisted and that it was permissible, the impeachment that occurred before the break, then we would ask that you admit the cross-examination portion of the transcript that was being used by the Prosecution because the only portions that were used with the witness were from the direct examination, and that leaves you with a partial view as to what the witness said in that previous statement, which is testimony. So that would be our request. If that request is denied, I can say that we would request some additional time, an adjournment, so that preparation can be made for further questions focusing on the relevant portions of the statement that was used by the Prosecution. So, Your Honours, that would be our submission and our request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think given the legal issues that are being raised that this should properly be briefed. If the Defence persists in this view, then it's our position that they should make the submissions in writing so that we can have also an opportunity to respond in writing and that the positions can be considered fully. So I don't think this is an issue that needs to be dealt with right now. I don't plan on using any more videos with the witness, and so I'm happy to move on to another topic and so that this can be addressed with more time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: May I make -- excuse me, Your Honour, may I make a proposal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- from the Prosecution side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: -- regarding the proposal by my colleague. The Prosecution would be prepared to have the Defence select the portions of the cross-examination that pertain just to the excerpts that I have addressed with this witness. So we don't object to, I think it's what Mr. Gosnell is proposing, I could be wrong, that the corresponding cross-examination that's relevant to what I showed Mr. Bogunovic can also be entered into evidence for impeachment purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I certainly wouldn't want to pre-empt Your Honours' decision, and I believe the first of the three potential remedies requested would obviate the need for any discussion of the resolution proposed to the second question, so I suppose I would -- I would simply ask that there be a ruling on the first remedy which was exclusion of the testimony that was heard relying on the prior testimony. And if Your Honours rule against that, then I could perhaps come back more specifically on the proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break to -- yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise for the intervention --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- because my colleague is obviously doing an outstanding job with this. I don't think we understood that an entire exclusion was a proposal or a remedy that was made in counsel's initial submissions. We understood that based upon the excerpt from the Appeals Chamber ruling - I think it was in Popovic - that first of all this is a matter for the Chamber's -- Trial Chamber's discretion, how it wants to handle all this, and that in order to inform the Chamber and perhaps place it in a position to more -- exercise its discretion in a more informed manner, to admit corresponding parts of the cross-examination to the extent that they may exist, we don't know, but to the extent that there is cross-examination that relates to those parts that the witness has spoken about, that those, from a Prosecution point of view, could be admitted or accepted for purposes of -- inform the Chamber's consideration how it wants to weigh all of these statements, both those made in the courtroom now today, yesterday, as well as those made previously in the Stanisic/Simatovic case. So we didn't understand that there was a proposal to exclude all of this. Maybe I misunderstood. We think that based on the very passage from Popovic, that's not a remedy that's justified or is certainly not compelled in that the Chamber can, in fact, consider any corresponding cross-examination, weigh all of it, and determine what use, if any, it wants to make from the statements made by the witness in the prior case. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell, do I understand -- I'm a bit confused as to your first proposal, but do I understand a part of your concerns, to use as vague a term as possible, to be that the -- you would need to be placed in the position to cross-examine the witness -- to further cross-examine the witness in respect of those, the corresponding portions of the transcript. And if that is -- my understanding is correct, how much time are we talking about in terms of -- because, of course, you're aware of the circumstances of the witness. I'm wondering how much time the very practical effects of that in terms of how do you see yourself being placed in the position of, you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Mr. President and Judge Hall, let me try to just respond very succinctly and concretely. As to the first remedy, I looked back at the transcript and I saw that I requested that you render a decision determining whether or not the manner in which the prior statements was used was permissible, and I did not expressly say that the consequence of a decision saying it was not permissible was that the portions of the testimony should be excluded from your consideration. I now make that express. That would be the request. Your Honours, I am well aware of the jurisprudence and the practice of this Tribunal that that's not a very likely outcome that Your Honours would reach, and therefore I propose two other remedies so that you would have that available for your consideration. The second remedy would be to permit us to tender the cross-examination portions of the Stanisic testimony. In principle, it's not -- the proposal by the Prosecution is perhaps reasonable. There might be discussions about what is the scope of what should be admitted in order to correspond to what has been presented to the witness, so there may be issues there and I wouldn't want to take a final position on that. Judge Hall, as to the third remedy and option, it would be that we be given sufficient time, because I know that Your Honours, on some occasions in the past, have had concerns about admitting large prior statements of a witness. And to respond to that concern, and given the fact that this was the extent of use of this prior -- of this prior testimony, my learned colleague would need some time to go through the Stanisic cross-examination to determine which portions are necessary to be put to the witness. Concretely, and I haven't had a chance to speak with my learned friend, but having gone carefully through that transcript myself, I can say that it would probably take at least a couple of hours, at least, in order to specifically determine which portions are relevant. And, of course, we'd also very much appreciate the videos from the Prosecution. If that could facilitate the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We will take a break to discuss in Chambers what the best course of action is. But before I do that, before I adjourn, Ms. Biersay, I did understand you well. If we continue Mr. Bogunovic's testimony, the redirect, you would move to another topic --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- to other topics?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I will not be showing any more of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, we are adjourned. --- Break taken at 11.20 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will allow the Defence to put to the witness those portions of his prior cross-examination from Stanisic and Simatovic as it considers necessary. Is the counsel able to do so immediately after the Prosecution's redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just to round this off, because during the break now the Prosecution has had an opportunity to read the decision that my learned friend had referred to, and just to note or perhaps to put on the record the Prosecution position that when it's all finished with the witness, when he's completed his testimony, that it's in our view -- or it's our position that the Chamber in its discretion, of course, if it wishes, will be able to consider the prior statements, whether on direct or from cross-examination, in the Stanisic/Simatovic case either for impeachment or as substantive evidence. And that's a point that's made clear in the Popovic decision by the Appeals Chamber that on that point, which is sort of the next question, perhaps, once the witness has completed his testimony, that is something that the Chamber has the discretion to consider the extent to which it will accept the prior statements either as impeachment or as substantive evidence. And it's the Prosecution position, of course, that the Chamber very -- might well wish to consider these as substantive evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The witness may be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, thank you for your patience. I will not be showing you another video. Instead, I have just one last segment to address with you. I want to direct your attention to this morning when counsel, Mr. Zivanovic, at page 2 of the transcript, said that he had information from a large part -- number of participants at the Velepromet meeting on the 20th, that it was chaired by a lieutenant-colonel of the JNA, who introduced himself as the commander of the city of Vukovar. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And when he asked if you could confirm it, you said "yes," that you confirmed that information about the lieutenant-colonel being present and chairing the meeting. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: So my -- one of my questions to you is: Who was this lieutenant-colonel of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant-colonel of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Who was present --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Sorry, who was present at the meeting, at the Velepromet meeting, with other --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I have nothing further at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, first I'm going to ask you about what happened in Borovo Selo, what you explained to the Prosecutor just now in response to the question that was put to you by them. Actually, that meeting with the Croatian representatives in Borovo Selo. You spoke about that yesterday as well. I can actually tell you exactly what page it was. What the transcript page was, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Biersay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: Sorry, perhaps I haven't understood the procedure, but I thought that the recross was going to be on the issue that we discussed earlier in the Court's ruling. Is this something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it -- this question are follow-up from the re-examination of the witness in respect of the meeting in Borovo Selo. For the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you have one or perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: One --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, just one question in this respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have a problem with that, Ms. Biersay?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I refer to the page 9143 of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You explained this -- or, rather, you spoke about this meeting. As far as I understood you, you said that it happened when Goran was arrested in Plitvice?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because in response to the Prosecutor's question you said that this happened in May to the best of your recollection. According to my information, Goran Hadzic was arrested in Plitvice on the 31st of March, 1991. So I wanted to ask you whether you stand by what you said, that it happened in May or, rather, that it happened at this other point in time? More specifically, that should be the first days of April.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you with 100 per cent certainty. It wasn't May. That's a mistake. Because there was no meeting on the 2nd of May because what happened happened. So it could have been only on the 1st of or 2nd of April when we had that meeting in Borovo Selo. The 2nd of May - how do I put this? - there was this attack against Borovo Selo or, rather, that gun-fire and everything else that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, now I'm going to put something to you, part of the answers that you provided in the Stanisic/Simatovic case. These are answers given to Defence counsel for Jovica Stanisic. In a way we believe that this could complete the questions that were put to you by the Prosecutor when showing you the video footage. I don't have the video, though, but I'm going to read out this text to you. It's in the English language and you are going to receive interpretation. So I'd kindly ask you to give me answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: I rise just for -- may I please have a page reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah. These are page 6007 through 6015, and 6040 to 6044.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIERSAY
utterances.text: And for the record, the first range is in tab 82, which is 65 ter number 4466. And I believe the second range is in tab 83, 65 ter 4467, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I read from the page 6007, line 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Mr. Jordash: Please go to paragraph 25. The B/C/S paragraphs correspond to the English paragraphs, so, yes, paragraph 25 in both the English and the B/C/S. "Q. And, Mr. Bogunovic, could you please look at the surrounding context because I want to understand precisely what it is you meant by this paragraph. "A. In this part of my statement I stated that I had no contacts with any person from the DB and that there isn't anything I could say on that topic." [Interpretation] Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: -- that you provided such an answer?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "Q. The investigator speaking to you in 2003, in relation to the DB was asking you about what role the DB had played in the events in the SBWS in 1991 and 1992; is that correct? "A. Yes, it is. "Q. And am I correct that your answer at paragraph 25 took into account both civilian and military matters concerning 1991 and 1992; is that correct? "A. I'm afraid I did not understand your question. Could you please repeat. "Q. The -- when you answered that the DB had -- let me start that again. When you stated that you had no contact with the DB, who were you referring to when you said that 'we had no contact with the DB?' Who was 'we?' "A. We of the government from the area. At least I'm not familiar with this. "Q. And when you say 'the government,' are you referring to -- just give me a moment. "A. The government of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. "Q. Were you also referring to the National Council which existed before the government? "A. Yes, I was. As of the 7th of January when the National Council was established in 1991 and onwards." [Interpretation] You remember those answers?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [In English] "Q. And were you referring to issues concerning the JNA when you stated that you did not know what role the DB had played? "A. No. The question was about the State Security Service, and I said what I said. I said that we had no contacts with them. As for the JNA, we did have contact with them, with the people who at that time were in the Sirmium-Baranja region. "Q. So you are saying that whatever the government or National Council was engaged in the SBWS, it had, as far as you were aware, no contacts with the DB of Serbia? "A. Yes, that's what I said. "Q. And putting aside your direct contacts, the government's direct contacts with the DB, were you also saying that you did not know what role the DB had played and you had not been told what role they might have played; is that correct? "A. Yes, it is. "Q. Do you stand by that answer today? "A. I do." [Interpretation] You remember those answers that you provided? You remember the questions and the answers?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "Q. I want to ask you about some of your activities. As paragraph 12 notes: "'As the minister of the interior, my first duty was to form the police station in the village of Borovo Selo and Dalj. Our task was to find people and choose those who would work there and also to provide them with uniforms, equipment, vehicles,' et cetera. "Are you with me, Mr. Bogunovic? "A. I am. "Q. Am I correct that your first duty was an urgent one because of the chaos which existed at that time in parts of the region of the SBWS. "A. I did not understand. I did not understand the question well. "Q. It is important that you moved quickly to form a police station in both Borovo Selo and Dalj because civilians of both ethnicities were being harassed by, let me put it generally, men with guns; is that correct? "A. Yes, it is. "Q. And so your task was an urgent one --"

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We just noted that the transcript page is the same on the screen. But I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I was trying to convey to you, Mr. Zivanovic, to go a little bit slower --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Slow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "And so your task was an urgent one and your task required supplies which you didn't at the time possess; is that correct? "A. It is."

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "Q. You were setting up police stations from scratch, if you understand that statement? "A. Yes. "Q. And so you -- "A. Correct. That's correct. "Q. And so you look towards the Novi Sad SUP to provide some of those supplies to enable you to set up police stations; is that correct? "A. Yes. "Q. And the SUP provided some basic supplies to allow you to set up police station; is that correct? "A. Yes, it is. "Q. And at paragraph 13 you state that part of those supplies included guns from the SUP Novi Sad; is that correct? "A. From the warehouse I specified. That's where --"

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: "That's where we received supplies from. It belonged to the SUP of Novi Sad. "Q. And were those supplies used by the police officers in the police stations that you refer to at paragraph 12 and 14? "A. Yes. "Q. And did those police stations as a general rule bring some law and order to the SBWS region, or certainly those villages referred to in your statement? "A. Yes, they did, not only in those villages but in the villages surrounding them." [Interpretation] You remember that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
